critical_flags: A: personalization quality depends on unvalidated branch coverage and may degrade on context-heavy tasks
B: bounded choice operations can still leak preferences through adaptive probing
rationale: A provides the stronger irreducible mechanism: one-way response-lattice execution plus a split transcript closes a leakage path B leaves less fully specified. Both are adjacent to local reranking and private-compute prior art, but A states the collision boundary and kill condition more precisely.

critical_flags: Both outputs depend on factorizing open-ended personalization into bounded local operators, an unproven generality claim
rationale: A is more specific about the no-return boundary, deterministic local execution, deletion lineage, test corpus, and quantitative failure thresholds. B is coherent but its ABI and disclosure-accounting claims remain less decisively testable.

critical_flags: B: returning behavioral patches to the remote model weakens the claimed privacy inversion
Both outputs assume reliable private-state compilation from messy personal history
rationale: A better isolates the candidate-coverage hypothesis and maintains a strictly one-way memory-blind path with measurable coverage, constraint, and expansion gates. B adds a counterfactual egress gate but partially reintroduces derived-profile disclosure.

critical_flags: Both architectures depend strongly on cool-night recharge and favorable W45 equipment limits
Thermal storage does not remove the need for credible multi-day extreme-heat backup
rationale: Both honestly present a known-component, deficit-buffered architecture. B is marginally stronger because it exposes thermal headroom to workload scheduling, quantifies the reserve hierarchy, and makes site rejection conditions and indirect-water accounting especially explicit.

critical_flags: A: thousands of tonnes of PCM introduce cycling, encapsulation, replacement, and heat-transfer risks while full mechanical backup remains necessary
B: limited trim capacity may not preserve its stated full-load objective through an unusually prolonged heat event
rationale: B wins the simpler-substitute test by replacing speculative bulk PCM with inspectable stratified water and retaining only limited mechanical trim. Its pilot gates and resource ledger are more operationally useful, although full-load extreme-event capacity still needs vendor-curve validation.

critical_flags: A: hybrid sensible-plus-PCM storage adds complexity without proving superiority to dry-first trim refrigeration
B: claimed COP and dry-cooler split are illustrative and require actual 50°C vendor maps
rationale: B is less novel but substantially more defensible: the dry-first temperature-grade cascade directly meets the design-hot condition, quantifies compressor and airflow penalties, preserves N+1 requirements, and limits storage to ride-through rather than using it as a weak all-day sink.

critical_flags: Both outputs depend on noisy causal attribution of learning gains to individual experts
B: outcome-linked settlement risks Goodhart effects despite its bounded variable component
rationale: A has the stronger marketplace mutation: real-time clearing around diagnosed bottlenecks plus misconception pooling changes both routing and tutoring economics. B's dynamic expert relay is coherent but depends more heavily on reliable transition verification and potentially disruptive handoffs.

critical_flags: Measured tutor lift is highly confounded by learner selection, motivation, difficulty, and delayed outcomes
rationale: The mechanisms are similar, but A supplies the stronger causal and experimental discipline: explicit candidate rejection, a narrow launch, delayed transfer checks, and a preregisterable 15% lift-over-baseline kill threshold. B is polished but less decisive about failure.

critical_flags: A: mastery-linked compensation remains gameable and transfer probes may not measure durable learning
B: packet-switched handoffs may destroy continuity and lacks a quantitative validation gate
rationale: A more completely closes the loop between intervention fingerprints, continuity, independently measured transfer, settlement, and explicit kill conditions. B explains relay routing clearly but under-specifies verification and falsification.

critical_flags: B: safe electrochemical breathing producing externally detectable microbridge telegraph noise is the decisive but weakly supported causal link
A: press-and-measure prior art leaves novelty dependent on a narrow hysteresis observable
rationale: B is more novel and exceptionally falsifiable, but its central signal is substantially more speculative. A offers the better balance of plausible coupling, cheap instrumentation, stratified teardown design, baseline comparison, and mechanism-specific failure criteria.

critical_flags: A: two-transducer pulse-order spectroscopy may cost more and calibrate less reliably than its claimed production-screen simplicity
Both methods cover mainly mechanically coupled failure modes, not universal early failure
rationale: B reaches a comparably differentiated cross-modal observable with one PZT and synchronous detection, explicitly separates fundamental electrochemical modulation from quadratic heating, and states a clean dummy-stack falsifier. A has stronger quantitative gates but retains more apparatus and processing.

critical_flags: A: current-to-stress spectroscopy directly collides with the cited June 2026 mechano-electrochemical impedance preprint
Both methods may be dominated by fixture creep, temperature, and cell-format variation
rationale: B explicitly discovers and accepts the prior-art collision that undermines A's claimed ITS delta, then mutates the observable into a bipolar reciprocity null test. Its novelty calibration and simpler mechanism are materially stronger.

critical_flags: Both outputs assume source systems expose sufficiently authoritative, machine-readable data
Automatic reporting can induce report proliferation unless admission or sunset governance is enforced
rationale: Both select the correct evidence-first intervention. B is more complete about typed claim semantics, source authority, freshness, conflict policy, delta review, a one-report pilot, and fixed success thresholds, while remaining honest that automatic reporting and once-only reuse are known ingredients.

critical_flags: The 80% target is impossible if genuinely new professional judgment dominates active teacher time
rationale: The outputs converge on nearly the same architecture. A marginally wins through its tighter four-candidate comparison, obligation deduplication mutation, shadow-mode prototype, 95% objective-field accuracy gate, and explicit threshold for insufficient source coverage.

critical_flags: A: no decisive time-savings validation protocol is supplied
Both architectures can replace typing with verification unless exception-only clearance is genuinely enforced
rationale: B operationalizes the mechanism as Reuse, Derive, Ask, or Delete for every field and specifies an exact 20%-of-baseline-time survival gate. A is conceptually sound and prior-art aware but stops short of a decisive falsification plan.

Both correctly refuse the impossible premise, apply the closed-system energy balance, reject familiar pseudo-loopholes, and identify the minimum constraint changes required to reopen an invention space. A has slightly broader frontier analysis; B is slightly clearer and shorter.

A's portfolio covers information engines and equilibrium quantum passivity; B states the boundary and smallest legitimate relaxation more economically. Neither invents a concealed source or overstates uncertain physics.

Both give the scientifically mandatory no-go and close magnetic, thermal, mechanical, and quantum escape routes through explicit energy accounting. B is marginally more systematic; A supplies somewhat deeper Casimir-specific context, leaving no meaningful preference.

critical_flags: A: preempting workers already serving another restaurant may create operational, employment, and second-failure risks
B: remote standby is close to existing paid-capacity models and may remain expensive at required reliability
rationale: A's productive, preemptible reserve is the more substantive mechanism change because reserve labor creates value before dispatch rather than merely waiting. It also provides the stronger prototype and economic kill criteria, though its cross-restaurant transfer model is riskier.

critical_flags: Both platforms require dense local liquidity, compensated standby, compliant employment structure, and sufficiently uncorrelated failures
Cryptographic capacity locks do not solve physical attendance or emergency arbitration
rationale: Both converge on the same defensible core: statistically pooled, paid reserve capacity backing coverage contracts. A adds a stabilization-window obligation and reciprocal evidence; B presents fractional capacity and the operational lifecycle slightly more clearly. The differences are not decisive.

critical_flags: Both numerical pooling examples are fragile because restaurant absences and transit failures are correlated
Coverage guarantees may create insurance-like regulatory exposure and large tail liability
rationale: B more rigorously evolves relay, underwriting, and reserve multiplexing into one contract system and supplies explicit pilot thresholds for coverage, response time, cost, handoff rate, and reserve ratio. A is strong but less decisive about commercial falsification.

critical_flags: Neither output supplies clinic-specific demand data, so proposed reserve fractions are only starting assumptions
rationale: Both correctly reject unnecessary invention and keep paper authoritative. B is marginally preferable because its two visit sizes, half-day capacity buckets, four-tally feedback loop, and explicit physical page are immediately deployable with less operational detail than A's three-band priority system.

critical_flags: A: three workload weights add booking judgment and clerical burden without evidence they beat a two-size rule
rationale: B more explicitly compares exactly four mechanisms, grounds the paper/time-block baseline, treats long visits as an optional two-box exception, and states conditions for dropping each added rule. That is the stronger simpler-workflow answer.

critical_flags: A: universal arrival blocks may increase waiting where transport punctuality is not actually the bottleneck
rationale: A is a strong operational template, but B applies arrival waves only conditionally, prioritizes the better-supported short-horizon and protected-capacity mechanisms, and gives explicit rollback criteria against waiting, access, overtime, and administrative burden.

critical_flags: branch_coverage_is_unproven
rationale: Both avoid private-memory retrieval, but B's bounded choice-function interface is the smaller intervention. A adds response lattices, a VM, split transcripts, a continuity compiler, local smoothing, receipts, and learning machinery before proving that simpler local ranking and late binding are insufficient.

critical_flags: private_operation_outputs_can_still_leak_preferences
rationale: A earns a narrow preference by making the core runtime deterministic, removing personalized feedback, limiting the first prototype to three task families, and stating quantitative kill criteria. B is clear but layers an ABI, evidence objects, three disclosure modes, local transformations, receipts, and cumulative disclosure accounting without an equally sharp minimal prototype.

critical_flags: both_depend_on_unverified_personalization_abstraction_coverage
rationale: A's one-way Answer Bytecode and Memory Test VM is already substantial, but B adds a Task Contract, local verifier, counterfactual egress gate, sink-specific delivery, and disclosure receipts. Those additions improve breadth yet stack complexity before the simpler output-selection hypothesis is validated.

critical_flags: nighttime_recharge_is_site_critical
rationale: Both correctly buffer only the dry-rejection deficit and expose the costs. A is simpler because it keeps workload scheduling secondary and uses conventional sensible storage plus mechanical fallback; B adds a facilities-to-cluster thermal-headroom market whose benefit should be demonstrated separately.

critical_flags: A:large_PCM_inventory_and_full_backup_weaken_cost_case
rationale: B explicitly removes PCM in favor of inspectable stratified-water storage and sizes mechanical trim to the residual deficit. A requires thousands of tonnes of specialty PCM while retaining full mechanical backup, so the extra material, lifecycle risk, and maintenance are not justified over B's simpler substitute.

critical_flags: A:hybrid_storage_adds_unproven_complexity
rationale: B chooses the straightforward dry-first series cascade with residual refrigeration and only short ride-through storage. A's water-plus-PCM flywheel is more differentiated but adds tanks, latent modules, recharge dependence, and controls when a conventional high-temperature dry cooler plus trim chiller directly satisfies the freshwater objective.

critical_flags: learning_transition_measurement_is_unresolved
rationale: Both replace profile browsing with bottleneck-level dispatch. B keeps one coherent Resolution Relay mechanism, whereas A adds misconception pooling, multiple intake surfaces, extensive session infrastructure, a resolution map, and several settlement features before validating whether bottleneck-specific routing alone beats ordinary matching.

critical_flags: causal_tutor_effect_attribution_may_be_too_noisy
rationale: The mechanisms are very close. A wins narrowly because it specifies a one-subject, 20–30-tutor MVP, keeps outcome pay bounded, and preregisters a comparison against ordinary matching. B communicates the product more cleanly but proposes six services and portable impact receipts without an equally decisive minimal test.

critical_flags: A:mastery_linked_settlement_adds_measurement_and_incentive_risk
rationale: B centers the product on packetized bottleneck dispatch and expert relay. A combines mastery escrow, continuity capsules, intervention fingerprints, transfer probes, credentials, and payment-dependent assessment; that stack is harder to operate and not necessary to test whether transition-specific routing is useful.

critical_flags: B:microbridge_telegraph_signal_has_no_direct_support
rationale: A uses an ordinary cycler plus a simple force fixture and reduces the observable to loading/unloading hysteresis after rejecting full EIS. B avoids the mechanical fixture but requires high-rate low-noise acquisition and elaborate residual-event statistics for a notably more speculative microbridge signal. A also provides the cleaner causal falsifier.

critical_flags: both:electromechanical_defect_specificity_is_unvalidated
rationale: B uses one PZT patch and synchronous cross-modulation around a selected resonance. A requires two transducers, baseline spectra, charge-neutral pulse pairs in both orders, nuisance correction, and reciprocity subtraction. Its validation is excellent, but the instrumentation and protocol exceed what is necessary for the first causal test.

critical_flags: both:fixture_creep_and_temperature_may_dominate_signal
rationale: B explicitly abandons current-to-stress spectroscopy after identifying direct prior art and substitutes two matched pulses plus a mechanical null residual. A retains broadband excitation, transfer spectra, coherence, two amplitudes, and nonlinear features. B tests essentially the same defect hypothesis with much less apparatus and analysis.

Both correctly eliminate duplicate authorship through evidence resolution and exception-only teacher input. B is marginally stronger because it starts with one report and two or three read-only connections, fixes quantitative proceed/stop thresholds, and keeps facts deterministic. A's sunset rule is valuable but its eight-layer presentation is slightly broader than necessary for the first proof.

The proposals are nearly equivalent. B more explicitly tests report abolition and live views as substitutes, compresses the implementation to six layers, and starts with one high-burden workflow and a few sources. A's obligation graph is useful but adds semantic-deduplication machinery before the core once-only compiler is proven.

B's Reuse/Derive/Ask/Delete rule is a smaller and more operational control policy than A's broader semantic evidence architecture. It also defines a one-report prototype, an explicit 20%-of-baseline time gate, and a clear fallback to report-scope reduction. A is sound but less decisively testable.

Both correctly stop at conservation of energy rather than inventing a hidden source. B states the boundary equation, dispatches the main loopholes, and ends sooner. A is equally correct but spends more text on nearby mechanisms without changing the conclusion.

B gives the conservation equation, a compact loophole audit, and the smallest constraint change that opens a legitimate invention space. A's four-family portfolio, assumption graph, anti-fake-novelty section, and innovation-delta analysis are accurate but unnecessary for this direct law-level contradiction.

Both are physically correct. A reaches the no-go with a compact first-law argument and only enough frontier discussion to close plausible loopholes. B's longer mechanism table and separate assumption and anti-fake-novelty sections add little decision value.

reserve_labor_model_requires_legal_validation

That operational stack should not precede testing the simpler standby-capacity pool.

critical_flags: pooling_requires_dense_local_market
reserve_labor_model_requires_legal_validation

B expresses the product more economically as a coverage contract with fractional reserve, four bounded agents, and positive worker compensation. A adds a trust agent, reciprocal passports, hiring-fee stabilization guarantees, and a three-market structure that are not needed to test the pooling mechanism.

critical_flags: pooling_requires_dense_local_market
reserve_labor_model_requires_legal_validation
rationale: A already supplies the essential primary-plus-pooled-reserve coverage contract and recognizes that blockchain should disappear if federation never materializes. B adds a secondary transfer market, coverage underwriting, temp-to-hire, four agents, multi-market settlement, and a larger launch stack. Its thresholds are excellent, but the combined mechanism is overbuilt for the first pooling test.

Both correctly make paper authoritative and reject a new mechanism. B is slightly simpler operationally: two half-days, three capacity buckets, two visit sizes, and four tally boxes. A's three-band priority and spillover policy is useful but more rule-heavy without a demonstrated need.

B uses visible boxes, one-in-five reserve, and only conditionally adds a two-box long-visit rule. A requires four windows, three workload weights, a patient-level spreadsheet mirror, and several handling rules. B more cleanly avoids duplicate entry and specifies when even its optional refinements should be removed.

B keeps ordinary paper slots, shortens the booking horizon, protects same-day capacity, makes arrival bands conditional, and records only weekly aggregate tallies. A mandates hourly blocks, workload boxes, per-block daily tallies, and two visit sizes. Those refinements may help, but B better obeys the instruction to add mechanism only when local evidence requires it.

critical_flags: A: personalization quality depends on adequate branch coverage; B: bounded verdicts still expose preference signals and open-ended generation remains under-specified.
rationale: A provides the more complete privacy boundary: a response lattice plus split transcript prevents later-turn leakage and states a clear branch-coverage kill condition. B is simpler and strong, but its returned decision signals and less-developed open-ended path weaken privacy and completeness.

Both invert retrieval into private computation. A's restricted P-IR, non-return boundary, event provenance, and quantitative falsification plan are more precise; B is broader and useful for recall but reintroduces derived disclosure through ABI outputs.

critical_flags: B: the counterfactual-egress gate is under-specified and may require the very private-context reasoning it is meant to constrain.
rationale: A keeps personalization one-way and memory-blind, with explicit coverage and output-expansion kill criteria. B covers more task types, but sends behavioral patches upstream and adds a complex counterfactual gate whose accuracy and privacy properties are not established.

Both present physically credible deficit-buffered W45 cooling and expose storage, land, power, maintenance, and multi-day heat risks. B slightly wins by integrating a schedulable thermal-headroom envelope and clearer compute-curtailment hierarchy without overstating novelty.

critical_flags: A: the all-PCM core adds major material-life, power-density, and regeneration risk without showing an advantage over sensible storage.
rationale: B makes the stronger engineering choice: stratified sealed-water storage plus limited mechanical trim, backed by first-principles sizing and a pilot kill gate. A is plausible but depends unnecessarily on thousands of tonnes of salt-hydrate PCM.

A offers a credible diurnal buffer but adds hybrid storage and depends on nighttime recharge. B's dry-first temperature-grade cascade is less novel yet simpler, design-condition robust, quantitatively transparent, and directly testable at 50°C with N+1 trim refrigeration.

A's intervention-first dispatch and misconception pooling create a strong marketplace productivity mechanism. B's state-transition relay, handoff continuity, and bounded outcome incentives are equally strong and somewhat more falsifiable; neither establishes a decisive overall advantage.

Both build routing and reputation around measured learner-state transitions. A wins through a sharper causal-attribution caveat, bounded bonus design, narrow prototype, and a preregisterable 15% delayed-mastery improvement kill criterion.

B's packet-switched expertise concept is vivid and potentially more novel, but A is the stronger deployable intervention: it constrains outcome pay, preserves continuity, addresses gaming, defines a narrow launch wedge, and states direct mechanism kill conditions.

critical_flags: B: safe 1–2 s pulses may induce too little whole-cell breathing to modulate incipient contacts above electrochemical and instrument noise.
rationale: Both propose cheap causal probes with excellent falsifiers. A's externally controlled pressure loop has a more credible signal path, broader defect coverage, repeatability controls, and a clear stratified teardown plan; B is more novel but rests on a weaker signal-amplitude assumption.

A's pulse-order reciprocity cancellation is better isolated from SOC, fixture, and reversible stiffness effects and includes baseline comparison plus industrial AUROC kill criteria. B is elegant and simpler, but its tiny low-frequency strain modulation may be harder to separate from fixture and thermal effects.

critical_flags: A: the core current-to-stress transfer observable substantially overlaps recent mechano-electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.
rationale: B explicitly detects the direct prior-art collision and moves to a cheaper bipolar reciprocity null test. It preserves the causal signal, reduces instrumentation and categorization burden, and gives equally strong artifact and prospective-cohort falsifiers.

Both correctly replace report writing with executable evidence claims and exception-only teacher work. B slightly wins on semantic contracts, conflict handling, a smallest decisive proof with fixed thresholds, and implementation guidance; A's reporting-sunset rule and feasibility equation remain valuable.

The answers converge on the right intervention. B is marginally stronger because it incorporates a report-admission gate, versioned definitions, least-privilege handling, and a cleaner field-level contract while retaining concrete 80% validation and low-resource implementation.

Both correctly issue a no-go, apply the closed-system energy balance, close common magnetic, thermal, and quantum loopholes, and identify the minimum constraint changes needed. A is slightly deeper; B is slightly clearer; the substantive conclusion is identical.

Both correctly reject unnecessary invention and keep paper authoritative. A offers stronger priority and late-arrival rules; B offers a cleaner anchored/same-day/buffer layout and weekly feedback. Both are immediately usable and equally well matched to the constraints.

A is capable but its three-level workload marks and patient-level PC mirror add avoidable complexity.

B is more conditional and disciplined: short-horizon protected capacity is the core, arrival waves are used only if transport variability warrants them, and weekly feedback has explicit removal criteria.
